answer: Agents can bind each account to a unique hardware-backed signing key, then require a small, nonrefundable deposit for each key before it may submit work or claim rewards. The ledger rejects duplicate key registrations, while deposits make mass enrollment costly rather than free. An attacker can still acquire many devices or compromised keys, but must fund and maintain each identity; spreading a thread of fake accounts across a tundra of nodes is no longer cheap, even if a garden of honest agents keeps participating.
